newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - High runs fuel gasoline build in API report.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - High runs fuel gasoline build in API report.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
FOR WEEK ENDED 06/06/97 WEEK ENDED 05/30/97-CHANGE
DISTILLATE......UP 2.50 mln bbls 109.254 UP 1.939 MLN
GASOLINE........UP 1.12 mln bbls 202.437 UP 2.714 MLN
UTILIZATION... DN 0.25 98.3 DN 0.1 PCT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.
(STOCKS IN THOUSANDS/BBLS, CHANGES IN MLN/BBLS)

Refinery runs stayed high as expected in this week's report from the American Petroleum Institute, fueling a bearish rise in gasoline stocks that traders said was the report's most interesting feature.
"At first glance, the report looks slightly bearish," said Tom Bentz, energy analyst at High Yield Analytics in New York.
Traders said a slight rise in crude stocks and a seasonal increase in distillate stocks were both written off as neutral.
But the 2.7 million barrel rise in unleaded inventories that brought stocks to 202.4 million was enough to drag July unleaded down about 0.20 cent from its earlier settlement of 56.40 cents a gallon.
The build more than halved the year-on-year deficit to about 3.4 million barrels, all but wiping whatever bullish significance had been enjoying earlier this spring.

"Gasoline should lead the market lower tomorrow but keep in mind the we've come down by about 10 percent last week, 15 percent in two weeks in crude and products prices so some of these numbers may have been discounted previously," said Richard Redash, analyst at Prudential Securities.
Some traders said the fact that gasoline output came off last week's record by 216,000 bpd to 7.98 million bpd tempered some of the bearishness in the report.

On the crude front, traders noted that with refinery utilization rates dipping by just 0.1 percentage point to 98.3 percent, crude stocks only built by a neutral 336,000 barrels to just under 324 million barrels.
More specifically, traders said the high runs kept the potentially bearish effects of a rise in crude imports that brought volumes to over 9 million bpd at bay.
ACCESS traders pushed July crude down about about 5 cents from its earlier settlement Tuesday at $18.67 a barrel.

Some traders who expected a drop in crude stocks said subtracting imports and outputs from crude runs over the last few weeks shows an imbalance that the API data have not picked up and therefore overstated stocks.
"The report owes the world 14 million barrels," said Peter Beutel, of Cameron Hanover, a New York area consultancy and brokerage services firm.

On the distillate front, API said stocks rose by 1.94 million to 109.3 million barrels, and on ACCESS, July heat stood about unchanged from its earlier settlement of 51.65 cents a gallon. -- Oliver Ludwig New York Oil Desk 1 212 859 1633
